sourceIndex.main: No retained full primary text found in assigned relevant indexes. PRlib returned catalog metadata only; the one official alternative failed (403). HOLD.
sourceIndex.coverage: Six literal groups and four whole prompt-answer-note triples are hashed below. Core key/effect remains unqualified.

literal.prompt: Какой акт ввёл в Российской империи всесословную воинскую повинность?

literalGroups.primaryGround: PRlib identifies an item titled Устав о воинской повинности and says it was approved on 1 January 1874 (L39), but the statute text was not returned. The universal-service effect remains unsupported. The correct label repeats the prompt wording.

literalGroups.literal: Устав о воинской повинности ввёл всесословную воинскую повинность. Его высочайше утвердили 1 января 1874 года.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The universal-duty and prior-recruit-system claims are not established by the catalog page or failed alternative. The proposed date sentence is supported by the catalog entry only.

literalGroups.literal: Жалованная грамота городам 1785 года определила устройство городского самоуправления.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The Presidential Library dates both charters to 1785 and describes the City Charter’s elected institutions and municipal self-government.

literalGroups.literal: «Кондиции» 1730 года пытались ограничить власть Анны Иоанновны.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The full source says the Conditions limited Anna Ioannovna’s independent decisions and that she publicly tore them up.

literalGroups.literal: Устав о воинской повинности высочайше утвердили 1 января 1874 года.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The revised note adds the statute’s official approval date, a concrete own-option fact beyond the prompt/key. Metadata only, not proof of substantive effect.

literalGroups.literal: Документы приняли 30 декабря 1922 года; они объединили РСФСР, ЗСФСР, БССР и УССР в СССР.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The retained full source says the documents were adopted on 30 December 1922 and united the four named republics; the proposed wording avoids saying the republics themselves signed.
